field_updates.detail: Figure 2 "Typical Forward Characteristics", TA = 25 C curve (third from left; order 150/75/25/0/-40 C), typical forward curve, vector-extracted read points (IF, VF): (0.002 A, 0.6232 V), (0.005 A, 0.6689 V), (0.01 A, 0.7087 V), (0.02 A, 0.7563 V), (0.05 A, 0.8469 V), (0.1 A, 0.9349 V), (0.2 A, 1.0487 V); residuals mV: [6.9, -2.3, -6.5, -7.2, 4.7, 9.1, -4.7] (rms 6.3, max 9.1) Method: Least-squares fit of VF = N*Vt*ln(IF/IS+1) + IF*RS (linear in N*Vt, N*Vt*ln IS, RS), Vt=25.69 mV at 25 C, over 2 mA to 200 mA (7 points; the plotted 25 C curve spans ~1 mA to ~0.3 A). Points read from the PDF vector path of the curve (not a raster), axis calibrated to the plot frame/decade grid lines. Curve is drawn as a filled outline; VF taken as the mean of the outline crossings at each current. N lands at the class maximum (2.2); residuals show curvature a single exponential cannot follow. Figure is shared by BAV16W and 1N4148W.

field_updates.detail: Figure 4 "Typical Total Capacitance" (f = 1 MHz), thick curve, mean of outline crossings, typical junction capacitance vs reverse voltage, read points (VR, C): (0.5 V, 0.746 pF), (1 V, 0.729 pF), (2 V, 0.714 pF), (5 V, 0.678 pF), (10 V, 0.650 pF), (15 V, 0.633 pF), (20 V, 0.618 pF), (30 V, 0.598 pF), (40 V, 0.584 pF); fit residuals %: [0.29, -0.39, 0.11, -0.27, 0.1, 0.35, 0.07, -0.09, -0.16] (max 0.39%) Method: Least-squares fit of ln C = ln CJO - M*ln(1+VR/VJ) (grid over VJ, linear solve for CJO and M at each VJ). Curve falls only from 0.76 to 0.58 pF over 0-40 V, so VJ/M are poorly separated (with VJ fixed at 0.4 or 0.7 V, M = 0.064 or 0.069 and CJO 0.79/0.78 pF fit within 1.1%). Consistent with CT max 2.0 pF at VR=0.

field_updates.detail: "Reverse Recovery Time tRR ... 4.0 ns IF = IR = 10mA, IRR = 0.1 x IR, RL = 100 ohm" (Max column) Method: Charge-control storage-time estimate used by the SPICE lumped-charge diode: ts = TT*ln(1+IF/IR). Treating the whole quoted trr as storage time gives TT = trr/ln(1+IF/IR). Ignores the recovery tail to the quoted Irr, junction capacitance and RS, so it over-estimates TT. TT <= 4 ns/ln 2 = 5.8 ns; upper bound from a maximum. Class default 23 ns would give ~16 ns, 4x the guaranteed maximum.
